tasks.description:
You are modifying the Nexus repository itself.

Your objective is to transform the existing DeepSeek Harness frontend into a distinct, polished Nexus-branded interface while preserving all current behavior.

## PRODUCT IDENTITY

The product name is:

NEXUS

Nexus is an AI engineering harness and deterministic development controller. It must feel like its own professional developer product, not a reskinned DeepSeek Harness.

The visual direction should resemble a premium modern developer tool such as Linear, Raycast, Cursor, or a restrained mission-control interface.

Avoid:

* gamer aesthetics
* excessive glow
* excessive gradients
* excessive glassmorphism
* large decorative elements
* unnecessary animations
* visual clutter

The interface should feel:

* technical
* precise
* compact
* premium
* calm
* powerful

## VISUAL SYSTEM

Target visual palette:

Main background:
#09090B

Sidebar:
#0D0D10

Surface:
#111116

Elevated surface:
#17171D

Border:
#27272F

Primary text:
#F5F5F7

Secondary text:
#A1A1AA

Muted text:
#71717A

Primary Nexus accent:
#7C5CFF

Primary accent hover:
#9177FF

Secondary accent:
#49C6E5

Success:
#32D583

Warning:
#F5A524

Error:
#F04438

These colors are DESIGN INTENT, not instructions to hardcode these values repeatedly.

Inspect the existing DSH theme architecture and map the design onto semantic theme tokens wherever possible.

Use:

* compact spacing
* approximately 8â€“10px surface radius
* subtle borders
* minimal shadows
* smooth 120â€“180ms transitions
* strong hierarchy
* existing/system typography unless there is a strong reason to change it

## BRANDING

Replace visible DeepSeek Harness / DSH branding with Nexus branding where this represents the host application.

Examples include:

* sidebar product identity
* application name
* browser title where practical
* favicon where practical
* visible default product labels

Do NOT rename upstream package names, APIs, internal identifiers, npm packages, or technical dependencies merely for cosmetic reasons.

The installed DeepSeek Harness is an implementation dependency. Nexus is the product presented to the user.

### Sidebar

The sidebar identity should become approximately:

[geometric Nexus mark] NEXUS

Do not permanently use the DeepSeek fish logo.

A simple temporary geometric mark is acceptable if a final Nexus SVG does not yet exist.

Prefer the existing official sidebar branding slots such as:

sidebar.brand.mark
sidebar.brand.name

over modifying the sidebar implementation directly.

## ARCHITECTURAL RULES

This requirement is critical.

DO NOT treat app/node_modules as Nexus source code.

You MAY inspect files under app/node_modules to understand the installed DeepSeek Harness UI.

You MAY patch generated/installed files as part of an automated installation step when no supported extension mechanism exists.

But all permanent Nexus customization logic MUST be stored in source-controlled Nexus files.

Use this priority order:

1. official DSH extension points / slots
2. theme tokens / supported configuration
3. Nexus-owned UI/plugin code
4. small deterministic post-install patches
5. direct upstream structural patching only when no cleaner option exists

Do not create fragile broad string replacements when a supported extension exists.

All patches must:

* be deterministic
* be idempotent
* fail clearly when the expected upstream structure changes
* never silently corrupt installed code

## INSTALLATION PERSISTENCE

A fresh Nexus installation must automatically recreate the branded UI.

Running npm ci must not permanently destroy Nexus customization.

Create an appropriate source-controlled structure, for example:

ui/
branding/
theme/
overrides/

and/or:

scripts/
Patch-NexusUi.ps1

The exact structure is your decision after inspecting the architecture.

Integrate the Nexus UI customization into the existing setup process AFTER dependencies are installed.

The installation flow should conceptually become:

install pinned runtime
â†’ npm ci
â†’ apply required Control Room compatibility patch
â†’ apply Nexus UI branding/theme customization
â†’ continue setup

Do not duplicate responsibilities that can be implemented using existing plugin/slot mechanisms.

## PHASE 1 SCOPE

This task is PHASE 1 only.

Implement:

1. Nexus application branding
2. Nexus sidebar branding
3. Nexus dark visual theme
4. buttons and interactive states
5. inputs and composer styling
6. cards / surfaces / dialogs where controlled by theme
7. active navigation state
8. hover state
9. focus state
10. consistent spacing and border treatment
11. application title/favicon if practical without fragile architecture
12. mode-selection UI styling so it visually belongs to Nexus

Do NOT implement major new functionality.

Do NOT yet add:

* controller telemetry panel
* task dashboard
* cost dashboard
* new routing logic
* new controller behavior
* major navigation architecture changes

Those belong to later Nexus UI phases.

## EXISTING FUNCTIONALITY

All existing behavior must remain operational, including:

* session creation
* workspace selection
* conversation UI
* mode switching
* Normal Engineering mode
* DeepSeek Only mode
* settings
* model synchronization
* existing Nexus controller integration
* launcher behavior
* DeepSeek execution
* optional Codex review
* restart behavior

A visual redesign is NOT allowed to regress functional behavior.

## UPSTREAM COMPATIBILITY

The pinned DSH version should remain the implementation base.

Before changing anything:

1. inspect the installed UI packages
2. identify the global theme architecture
3. identify existing branding slots
4. identify where application metadata/title/favicon originates
5. identify which desired changes require patches and which do not

Document these decisions briefly.

Do not guess upstream paths or structures.

## IMPORTANT EXISTING INSTALLER ISSUES

Be aware of previous fresh-install problems:

* the portable Node runtime needs to be available on PATH for npm lifecycle scripts that invoke bare `node`
* PowerShell CRLF vs installed JavaScript LF can break exact multiline patch matching

Do not reintroduce either problem.

Any new patch logic must normalize or otherwise safely handle line endings.

## IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY

Prefer a small maintainable Nexus customization layer over a large fork.

Where possible, expose values centrally so future Nexus redesigns do not require modifying many files.

Avoid scattered magic values.

Keep branding/theme logic separated from controller/runtime logic.

Do not modify unrelated backend/controller behavior.

## VERIFICATION

After implementing the redesign:

Run all relevant existing Nexus tests.

Also verify at minimum:

* Nexus setup logic still succeeds
* Nexus branding customization is applied
* branding patch can be run twice safely
* DeepSeek fish is not used as the visible Nexus brand fallback
* NEXUS is visible as the application identity
* mode switching still works
* Normal Engineering still launches
* DeepSeek Only still launches
* settings still open
* session creation still works
* no startup errors are introduced

If practical, add deterministic checks to aih-doctor or the existing test suite that verify the Nexus UI customization is installed.

## WORKFLOW

Before editing:

1. inspect relevant code
2. map requested changes to existing DSH extension points
3. state a concise implementation plan
4. make the smallest maintainable implementation
5. run targeted verification
6. inspect git diff
7. fix regressions before declaring completion

Do not rewrite large upstream UI packages unless necessary.

## SUCCESS CRITERIA

This task is complete when:

* the application visually identifies as Nexus, not stock DeepSeek Harness
* the DeepSeek fish is no longer the visible product mark
* the application has a coherent Nexus dark visual system
* functionality is unchanged
* customizations survive reinstall / npm ci through Nexus-owned source-controlled logic
* patches are deterministic and idempotent
* tests pass
* the implementation is maintainable enough to continue with Phase 2 later

When finished, provide:

1. architecture decisions made
2. files added
3. files changed
4. how branding is applied
5. how theme customization is applied
6. which upstream areas still require patches
7. verification performed
8. any limitations remaining for Phase 2
